newsitem.title: USA: Great Western rejects Ahmanson stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Great Western rejects Ahmanson stock swap.

text.p: Great Western Finanical Corp. said Tuesday it has rejected a hostile takeover bid by H.F. Ahmanson & Co. because it is not in the best interests of the company and its stockholders.
The board, by unamious vote of those directors present, recommended that stockholders reject Ahmanson's proposal and not tender their shares to Ahmanson, Great Western said.
Ahmanson, the parent of Home Savings of America, one of the nation's largest consumer banks, is offering up to 1.2 of its shares for each Great Western share.

Ahmanson has been trying to delay a shareholder vote on Washington Mutual Inc.'s proposal to give the Great Western board a chance to hear from any new boardmembers that are elected at Great Western's annual meeting on June 13.
Ahmanson, parent of Home Savings of America, is seeking to have three directors elected to the board.

Great Western, based in Chatsworth, Calif., agreed to merge with Washington Mutual in a $6.5 billion deal in early March. The deal calls for Washington Mutual to exchange 0.9 of its shares for each Great Western share.

Great Western also said its board reaffirmed its determination that the terms of the company's definitive merger agreement with Washington Mutual are fair to, and in the best interests of, Great Western and its stockholders.

"In sharp contrast to Ahmanson's unsolicited proposal, our merger with Washington Mutual makes compelling economic and strategic sense for Great Western stockholders," Great Western said in a statement.
"We remain strongly committed to our merger with Washington Mutual and look forward to the June 13 stockholder vote."
Great Western's stock fell 12.5 cents to $47, while Ahmanson slid 37.5 cents to $41.125 early on the New York Stock Exchange. Washington Mutual fell 37.5 cents to $55.50 on Nasdaq.
